title: Ample extensions of powers of symmetric lines on the abelian open
statement: Let $T$ be a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $q:H\to T$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. A commutative group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group identities and commutativity; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Every geometric fibre is semiabelian: over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$ it fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves of commutative groups $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to H_k\to A\to1$, for some integer $r\geq0$ and a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme $A$ (an abelian variety); here $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication. Let $V\subseteq T$ be a dense open [def-weil-open-immersion] over which $H_V\to V$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence an abelian scheme. Let $M$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on $H_V$, with a rigidification $e_V^*M\simeq\mathcal O_V$, and suppose $[-1]^*M\simeq M$ (symmetry). Module pullback is tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. Assume $M$ is relatively ample: it is ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. There exists an affine open covering $T=\bigcup_iT_i$ such that, for each nonempty $T_i$, there are an integer $n_i\geq1$ and a rigidified invertible module $B_i$ on $H_{T_i}$ which is relatively ample over $T_i$, together with a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $B_i|_{H_{V\cap T_i}}\simeq M^{\otimes n_i}|_{H_{V\cap T_i}}$. In particular $B_i$ is ample on $H_{T_i}$. This is an existence theorem: no line module on all of $H$ is supplied as input.

source.place: XI Theorem 1.13, symmetric ample power-extension assertion, used in Moret-Bailly, Pinceaux de varietes abeliennes, VI Proposition 3.1, connected-fibre case. Original local WANTED; normal semiabelian formulation and local rigidification made explicit by Q124, agent responsibility.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semiabelian-cubical-rigidification](a) to the abelian scheme $H_V\to V$ and the given rigidification of $M$. The group is smooth separated of finite presentation with geometrically connected fibres by the hypotheses, and is proper over $V$. We obtain the unique compatible cubical structure on $M$; it preserves the prescribed rigidification.

source.place: I 2.6, abelian-scheme theorem of the cube.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-symmetric-cubical-extension] with $S=T$, $G=H$, $U=V$ and the cubical line $M$ from step 1. The base is normal integral Noetherian, the morphism has the stipulated semiabelian fibres, and $V$ is dense. Symmetry of the underlying module is exactly the hypothesis $[-1]^*M\simeq M$. Obtain a cubical rigidified line $B$ on $H$ and a rigidification-preserving isomorphism $B|_{H_V}\simeq M$. This application supplies an extension of $M$ itself.

source.place: II 3.3, extension of symmetric cubical lines.

proof.text: Because $T$ is integral and $V$ is dense open, its generic point $\eta$ lies in $V$. Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change] to $H_V\to V$, its relatively ample line $M$, and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\to V$. The target is affine, so $M_\eta$ is ample. The isomorphism of step 2 identifies $B_\eta$ with $M_\eta$; hence $B_\eta$ is ample and symmetric. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], applied to $H_V\to V$ and the same map, $H_\eta$ is proper.

Apply [lem-sfb-normal-cubical-generic-ampleness] to the supplied cubical line $B$ of step 2. Its base and group hypotheses are precisely those checked in step 2, and step 3 verifies properness of the generic fibre and ampleness and symmetry of $B_\eta$. Thus $B$ is relatively ample over $T$.

source.place: VI 3.1, normal connected-fibre cubical ampleness criterion.

proof.text: Take the one-member affine open covering $T_1=T$, the integer $n_1=1$, and $B_1=B$. The rigidified isomorphism in step 2 is the required one to $M^{\otimes1}\simeq M$. Relative ampleness includes ampleness on the inverse image of the affine open $T$ itself, which is $H$. These choices give every asserted clause.

Small cases checked: a DVR, a constant E x S over a normal cone (a non-symmetric degree-0 line does not extend, so symmetry is needed), and an affine G_m special fibre. Steps 1-5 check hypothesis by hypothesis: eta lies in V, ampleness of M_eta comes from Tag 0893 applied to Spec kappa(eta), and n=1 with the single cover {T} is a stronger conclusion while the statement is unchanged. There is no cycle; the parent regular-group node is not cited, and the new ampleness node generalises it. No repair note, no SGA. Batch 5: lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-base-change is the general Stacks 0893 lemma, outside both assumptions and not part of their proofs, so it is accepted.
